title: Blocked Due to Server Probe Failure

blocks.text: This runbook article describes how to resolve a triggered policy action when the Zscaler Service Edge cannot successfully connect to the target website that triggered the policy action via TCP or TLS. This happens when a web server either does not tolerate SSL Inspection or doesn't complete the TCP handshake with the Zscaler Service Edge.
Verify that you can access the website from a test system with direct access to the internet. Validate the SSL configuration of the web server in question.

blocks.heading: Use an External Tool to Validate the Server's SSL Configuration

blocks.text: To learn more, see How to Validate the SSL Configuration of a Web Server.
Review your organization's SSL Inspection policy for the concerned transactions.

If you have selected the action in the SSL Inspection policy as Do Not Inspect and Evaluate Other Policies, this error can still be displayed when the domain part of a URL is configured to be blocked in an access control policy, because the Zscaler service must decrypt a blocked transaction in order to show the End User Notification.
The following items are possible solutions for the issue:

blocks.item: If your business permits SSL Inspection for this domain, you can disable the option Block Undecryptable Traffic in the SSL Inspection rule for the domain with the action set to Inspect. To learn more, see Configuring SSL Inspection Policy.
As a workaround, you can also set the action in the rule to Do Not Inspect and Bypass Other Policies.
If none of these steps help, submit a case to Zscaler Support with the following information:

If you have enabled Remote Assistance, provide the complete URL in question, and the timestamp when a user tried accessing it via the Zscaler service. Otherwise, send the Web Insights logs showing all the columns for the relevant transactions.
If Zscaler Client Connector is installed, a client packet capture.
